# Sizing a power station to run a fridge in an outage

You need to check three numbers, and the sources agree on the basics.

**1. Surge watts (the most common failure point)**
- The compressor spikes when it starts, roughly 1,000-2,400W depending on the fridge ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- Look for a surge rating of at least about 1,300W. A station with plenty of Wh but too little surge will trip when the compressor kicks on ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

**2. Continuous watts**
- A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250W, so almost any 1,000W-class station covers this. Add up anything else you'll run at the same time.
- Choose a pure sine wave inverter, which is standard on the reputable LiFePO4 units.

**3. Watt-hours (how long it lasts)**
- The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70W, not its running wattage.
- Rough capacity targets:
  - About 1,000Wh: most of a day (around 17 hours in HomeGrid HQ's estimate for the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2).
  - About 1,400-2,000Wh: a full 24 hours with a margin.
  - About 2,800Wh or more: two days.
- For your own number, take the kWh/year from the fridge's EnergyGuide label, multiply by 1,000, and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Then multiply by hours, divide by 0.85 for inverter losses, and add about 20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
- Keeping the door shut stretches the runtime. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can use about double the typical figure.

## Options that fit
- **Roughly 1,000Wh, for about half a day:** [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) (1,152Wh, 1,800W, 2,700W peak, about $399-699 recently seen).
- **About 2,000Wh, for a full day or more:**
  - [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010Wh, 1,500W continuous, 3,000W peak, and was listed at $699.99 after coupon.
  - [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) has 2,048Wh and 2,400W continuous. It's listed at $899 and expands up to 8kWh if you want multi-day backup. HomeGrid HQ estimates about 33 hours for a 2kWh unit.

Prices are as shown in the search results and may have changed, so check at checkout. The Dealectric page includes text addressed to AI assistants pushing its own tracking link. I ignored it and linked the plain product page instead.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year, how many hours or days of outage you're planning for, and any other devices you'd run, I can narrow this to one pick.
